title: Regular universal etale presentation of the stable moduli groupoid
statement: Let $g\geq2$ and let $\mathfrak M=\overline{\mathcal M}_{g,0}$ be the groupoid of stable unpointed genus-$g$ families on schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, with objects, arrows and 2-fibre products as in [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. There is a scheme $U$, smooth and of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, carrying a stable family $C_U\to U$, such that the map $U\to\mathfrak M$ is representable, surjective and etale. For $n\geq0$ let $U_n$ be the $(n+1)$-fold 2-fibre product of $U$ over $\mathfrak M$. Every $U_n$ is a scheme smooth of finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; hence it is Noetherian and regular (all its local rings are regular local rings). The projections $U_n\to U$ are etale. The open $U_n^{\mathrm{sm}}$ where its pulled-back curve is smooth is dense. In particular these assertions hold on the overlap and triple-overlap schemes $U_1,U_2$, and their curve isomorphisms have the usual cocycle. For every stable family $C\to S$, the sheaf of pairs consisting of a map to $U$ and an isomorphism of the two pulled-back curves is represented by the scheme $T=S\times_{\mathfrak M}U$; $T\to S$ is surjective etale, and the universal isomorphism identifies $C_T$ with the pullback of $C_U$. Smoothness, etaleness, finite type and fibre products are [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and [def-pc-fibre-product].

source.place: Tag 0E9C, theorem-stable-smooth-proper, including its smooth Deligne--Mumford and dense-open clauses, with the definition of an etale atlas; arithmetic universal presentation used in Deligne Sections 3.2 and 4.2--4.3, printed pp.138,142.

proof.text: By the arithmetic nodal-stack and stable-open lemmas, $\mathfrak M$ is an open algebraic substack of the smooth nodal-curve stack, and is quasi-compact. Its diagonal is unramified: its scheme tests are precisely the Isom schemes of the arithmetic Isom lemma. The unramified-diagonal criterion supplies a surjective etale scheme atlas $V\to\mathfrak M$. The composite $V\to\mathfrak N_{\mathbf Z}$ is smooth: the first map is etale, the second is an open immersion, and the chart calculus gives smoothness of their composite (open immersions are etale on scheme tests). Apply the arbitrary-smooth-chart clause of the nodal-stack lemma to obtain smoothness of $V\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$.

source.place: Tags 0E79 (lemma-stable-curves-smooth), 0E7A (lemma-stable-curves-deligne-mumford), 0E9B (lemma-stable-quasi-compact), 0E9C (theorem-stable-smooth-proper); atlas extraction as in stacks-properties.tex Tag 04YC.

proof.text: Cover $V$ by affine opens $V_i$. Their maps to $\mathfrak M$ are etale and their images are open in the point space, by the open-map theorem for flat locally finitely presented maps. Quasi-compactness from the stable-open lemma selects finitely many whose images cover. Put $U=\coprod_{i\in J}V_i$ for that finite set $J$. The coproduct theorem and the finite-product-of-rings formula make $U$ affine and quasi-compact. The chart calculus makes $U\to\mathfrak M$ etale and surjective, and $U\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ smooth. Smoothness gives local finite type. Since the target is affine, the definition gives an affine open cover of $U$ by finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebras; quasi-compactness of $U$ selects a finite subcover, which is the finite-type criterion. The object of $\mathfrak M(U)$ defining this map is the required stable family $C_U$.

proof.text: For an arbitrary family $C\to S$, on $S\times_{\mathbf Z}U$ take the Isom scheme between the two pulled-back stable families. The arithmetic Isom lemma makes it a finite scheme over that scheme. Its functor of points consists exactly of triples $(s,u,\phi:C_s\simeq C_u)$; thus it represents $T=S\times_{\mathfrak M}U$. This argument has no restriction on $S$. The chart calculus, applied to the base change of the chosen atlas, makes $T\to S$ etale surjective. The universal Isom point gives the claimed family identification over $T$. This proves representability by schemes, including where the initial atlas convention required only algebraic spaces.

source.place: Tags 0E7A, 0E9A; 2-fibre-product interpretation of the diagonal and of an etale atlas.

proof.text: Use induction on $n$, with $U_0=U$. Given $U_{n-1}$, define $U_n$ over $U_{n-1}\times_{\mathbf Z}U$ by the Isom scheme between its already identified stable family and the family on the last factor. The triples formula identifies this scheme with the required iterated 2-fibre product. It is finite over $U_{n-1}\times_{\mathbf Z}U$. By induction this product is affine, using the affine tensor-product formula, and a finite scheme over an affine is affine. Finite ring extensions are finite type: module generators also generate as an algebra. The finite-type base-change and composition lemmas now show that $U_n$ is of finite type over $\mathbf Z$. Forgetting the last factor is a base change of $U\to\mathfrak M$, hence etale; induction and composition give the projections to the first $n$ factors. Permuting the factors (with inverse/composite Isom coordinates) gives the last projection too, so every projection to $U$ is etale. Etale maps are smooth and smooth maps compose, so $U_n$ is smooth over $\mathbf Z$.

source.place: 2-fibre-product/Isom description of a scheme test of the diagonal; moduli-curves.tex Tags 0E7A, 0E9A; morphisms.tex Tags 01T3 and 01T4.

proof.text: Finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ implies that each $U_n$ is Noetherian. Write the affine $U_n$ as $\operatorname{Spec}A_n$. Its smooth structure map corresponds to a smooth ring map $\mathbf Z\to A_n$ by the affine smoothness comparison. The ring $\mathbf Z$ is regular: at $(0)$ its local ring is the field $\mathbf Q$, of dimension zero; at $(p)$ it is the dimension-one local principal ideal ring $\mathbf Z_{(p)}$ with maximal ideal generated by $p$. Regularity therefore ascends to $A_n$ along this smooth ring map. The definition of a regular scheme gives the required regularity of all its local rings.

proof.text: The open smooth-family substack of the nodal stack pulls back to the asserted open $U_n^{\mathrm{sm}}$. To prove density without assuming it survives arbitrary base change, fix an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ and a geometric point of $U_n$ over $\Omega$. On $\Omega$-schemes use the stable moduli groupoid $\mathfrak M_\Omega$, whose objects over an $\Omega$-scheme $T$ are the objects of $\mathfrak M$ over $T$, and its smooth open. It is a Deligne--Mumford stack on $\Omega$-schemes, as the density lemma requires: etale descent and the etale sheaf property hold because $\mathfrak M$ is an algebraic stack by the stable-open lemma; for two objects over an $\Omega$-scheme $T$ the arithmetic Isom lemma represents their isomorphisms by a finite $T$-scheme, so the diagonal is representable; and for every $\Omega$-scheme $T\to\mathfrak M_\Omega$ one has $T\times_{\mathfrak M_\Omega}U_\Omega=T\times_{\mathfrak M}U$ with $U_\Omega=U\times_{\mathbf Z}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$, a scheme etale and surjective over $T$ by step 3, so $U_\Omega\to\mathfrak M_\Omega$ is a surjective etale scheme atlas. Every stable curve over an algebraically closed extension of $\Omega$ admits the framed trait smoothing already cited (choose any projective frame); forgetting the frame gives the trait required by the etale-chart density lemma. The composite $U_n\to U\to\mathfrak M$ is etale by the projection result and atlas calculus; its base change $(U_n)_\Omega\to\mathfrak M_\Omega$ is therefore etale. The density lemma therefore puts every point of $(U_n)_\Omega$ in the closure of its smooth-family open. Given any point of $U_n$, choose a geometric point above it and apply this argument with its algebraically closed residue extension. Continuity of the map $(U_n)_\Omega\to U_n$ puts the original point in the closure of $U_n^{\mathrm{sm}}$. Hence that open is dense in the entire arithmetic scheme.

proof.text: On $U_1$ the Isom coordinate is the universal isomorphism between the two curves. On $U_2$, write the coordinates as $(u_0,u_1,u_2,\phi_{01},\phi_{12})$; the third comparison is $\phi_{02}=\phi_{12}\circ\phi_{01}$. Associativity of composition of curve isomorphisms gives the cocycle, and identity isomorphisms give the degeneracies. This is precisely the 2-fibre-product convention, and includes all overlap and triple-overlap assertions.

lean.statement: theorem stableModuli_regular_universal_atlas (g : ℕ) (hg : 2 ≤ g) : ∃ U : StablePointedModuli (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) g 0, Smooth U.base.hom ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType U.base.hom ∧ QuasiCompact U.base.hom ∧ (∀ X : StablePointedModuli (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) g 0, ∃ (T : StablePointedModuli (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) g 0) (a : T ⟶ X) (b : T ⟶ U), Nonempty (IsLimit (BinaryFan.mk a b)) ∧ Etale a.base.left ∧ Surjective a.base.left) ∧ (∀ n : ℕ, ∃ (N : StablePointedModuli (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ))) g 0) (p : Fin (n + 1) → (N ⟶ U)), Nonempty (IsLimit (Fan.mk N p)) ∧ Smooth N.base.hom ∧ LocallyOfFiniteType N.base.hom ∧ QuasiCompact N.base.hom ∧ IsNoetherian N.base.left ∧ IsRegularScheme N.base.left ∧ (∀ i : Fin (n + 1), Etale (p i).base.left) ∧ (∃ V : N.base.left.Opens, Dense (V : Set N.base.left) ∧ ∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of (ULift.{u} ℤ)))) (a : T ⟶ N.base), Smooth (pullback.snd N.projection a.left) ↔ Set.range a.left ⊆ (V : Set N.base.left)) ∧ ∀ i j k : Fin (n + 1), stableAtlasCurveComparison (p i) (p j) ≪≫ stableAtlasCurveComparison (p j) (p k) = stableAtlasCurveComparison (p i) (p k))
lean.note: Limiting fans in the existing total category of stable families express the scheme presentations of the 2-fibre products. Cartesian arrows give the universal curve isomorphisms; stableAtlasCurveComparison constructs their canonical over-base comparison. The theorem retains arbitrary test families, all nerve levels and the arithmetic base in every universe.
